1. Introduction 47
48
The Amazon region has historically been the target of economic and strategic interest 49
due to its mineral, biological, and ecosystem service resources (Filho et al., 2025). This scenario 50
poses an imminent danger to its preservation and the maintenance of the lives and customs of 51
the traditional Amazonian populations (Flores et al., 2024; Barreto et al., 2025; Filho et al., 52
2025). 53
In recent decades, there has been a dizzying increase in mineral exploration in South 54
America, mainly rudimentary and illegal gold mining ( garimpo). Approximately 91% of this 55
exploitation occurs within the Amazon Brazilian, and 62% of that total is located in indigenous 56
territories, mainly in Kayapo, Munduruku and Yanomami ethnic groups communities. The 57
Brazilian Amazonian states of Amazonas, Mato Grosso, Pará and Rondônia are the most 58
affected by garimpo activity (Neto et al., 2024). 59
In the Amazon, garimpo activity is one of the most important sources of mercury (Hg) 60
emissions to atmosphere, soil and water bodies, and consequently the most important source of 61
contamination of the Amazonian rivers and their tributaries (Neto et al., 2024; Nevado et al ., 62
2010; Crespo-Lopez et al ., 2021; Teixeira et al. , 2021; Crespo-Lopez et al ., 2024). When 63
released into the environment, such as through its use in garimpo for gold amalgamation, 64
metallic mercury (Hgº) can be transported and redistributed in the atmosphere, soil and aquatic 65
systems (Crespo-Lopez et al., 2024). In rivers and sediments, some of the inorganic mercury 66
(IHg) can be methylated by methanogenic bacteria and become bioavailable, giving rise to 67
methylmercury (MeHg), the most toxic form with a high capacity for bioaccumulation along 68
the food chain (Gao et al., 2022; Crespo-Lopez et al., 2024). 69
The impacts of MeHg exposure disproportionately affect traditional Amazonian 70
populations, such as indigenous peoples and riverside communities, because their livelihoods 71
largely depend on fishing and consuming fish from contaminated rivers (Nevado et al ., 2010; 72
Vasconcellos et al., 2021; Crespo-Lopez et al. , 2021; Martoredjo et al., 2024) . The 73
biomagnification of MeHg in the aquatic food chain can alter the average proportion of this 74
element relative to total mercury (THg) in fish tissues, and can reach up to 95% (Malm et al ., 75
1995). Indeed, contamination and biomagnification by MeHg in fish from different trophic 76
levels in the Brazilian Amazon region was evidenced in a meta-analytic study, which evaluated 77
the contamination scenario reported by experimental studies developed between 2017 and 78
2022, including the states of Amazonas, Pará, Rondônia and Roraima (Pierezan et al. , 2024). 79

This scenario is particularly worrying because it exposes local populations to an imminent risk 80
of chronic contamination. 81
The effects of Hg toxicity on the human body include damage to the brain (with 82
cognitive, sensory and motor repercussions), bone marrow, kidneys, lungs, heart, reproductive 83
system, DNA damage and cancer promotion (Wu et al., 2024; Kang et al ., 2024 ). There is 84
particular concern for pregnant women, as MeHg can be easily transferred to the fetus through 85
the placenta. Furthermore, it can also be transferred to babies and children through breast milk, 86
making them a more vulnerable group due to their neurodevelopmental stage (Grandjean et al., 87
1998; Wu et al., 2024). 88
Studies have shown widespread Hg contamination in urban populations, gold miners, 89
riverside communities (Malm et al ., 1995; Nevado et al., 2010; Martoredjo et al., 2024 ) and 90
indigenous groups of the Munduruku, Kayabi, Kayapó and Yanomami ethnicities who live near 91
garimpo areas in the Amazon (Basta et al., 2021; Martoredjo et al., 2024; Hofer et al ., 2025; 92
Pinheiro et al ., 2025 ). The effects of such exposition and contamination become explicit in 93
indigenous and riverside populations, where they have already been associated with 94
neurological clinical manifestations (motor, sensory, cognitive and psychosocial disorders) in 95
adults, as well as impaired motor development, cognitive deficits, short stature and anemia in 96
children (Hoshino et al., 2015; Kempton et al., 2021; Pinheiro et al., 2025). 97
Hg transit routes (toxicokinetics) in the human body involve pathways related to 98
absorption, distribution, biotransformation and excretion, in which genes linked to the metal 99
conjugation and elimination, such as glutathione antioxidant system (e.g., GCLC, GCLM, GST 100
and GPX), metalloproteins and membrane transporters (e.g., ATP -binding cassette ( ABC) 101
transporters) participate (Gundacker et al., 2010; Llop et al ., 2014; Kang et al ., 2024). 102
Interestingly, in the Amazonian population, the toxic effects of Hg and its clinical 103
manifestations can be potentiated by the presence of polymorphisms in genes related to Hg 104
metabolism (Arrifano et al., 2018; Barcelos et al., 2013; Barcelos et al., 2015a; Barcelos et al., 105
2015b; Carvalho et al., 2024; Klautau-Guimarães et al., 2005; Lopes-Araújo et al., 2023; Marco 106
et al., 2011; Marco et al., 2012; Oliveira et al., 2014; Perini et al., 2021; Rocha et al., 2016; 107
Silva et al., 2023; Silva et al., 2024; Maraslis et al., 2025). 108
Studies in riverside populations have associated these polymorphisms (e.g., ALAD, 109
APOE, GSTM1, GSTT1, GSTP1, SLC6A15, TXNRD and eNOS) with increased susceptibility 110
to contamination, body retention and clinical manifestations of Hg toxic effects, such as 111
cognitive deficits, memory and attention impairments, peripheral neuropathy, motor and 112
sensory disorders, reduced nitric oxide bioavailability, increased cardiovascular risk, Hg-related 113

dyslipidemias, higher prevalence of hypertension and increased risk of acute myocardial 114
infarction (Arrifano et al., 2018; Barcelos et al., 2013; Barcelos et al., 2015a; Barcelos et al., 115
2015b; Lopes-Araújo et al., 2023; Marco et al., 2011; Marco et al., 2012; Oliveira et al., 2014; 116
Maraslis et al., 2025). Similarly, in various indigenous ethnic groups, studies have associated 117
these polymorphisms (e.g., ABCB1, ABCC2, ALAD, GSTM1, GSTT1 and GSTP1) with 118
increased susceptibility to metal contamination and retention, and clinical manifestations such 119
as cognitive deficits, somatosensory alterations, distal peripheral neuropathy, motor disorders, 120
visual field alterations, hypertension and delayed neurodevelopment in children (Carvalho et 121
al., 2024; Klautau -Guimarães et al., 2005; Perini et al., 2021; Silva et al., 2023; Silva et al., 122
2024). Therefore, there is a significant amount of research that has assessed the impact of 123
genetic polymorphisms in genes related to Hg metabolism in traditional Amazonian 124
populations; however, this information remains scattered and lacks consistent meta -analytic 125
analysis. 126
In this study, we conducted a systematic review that provides a current overview of the 127
impacts of these polymorphisms on the clinical manifestations induced by Hg poisoning in 128
traditional Amazonian populations. Furthermore, we developed a meta -analysis in order to 129
strengthen the relationship between these polymorphisms and increased susceptibility to Hg 130
contamination. Finally, we performed a functional analysis using all polymorphic genes, 131
demonstrating that they are closely related to metal detoxification. Our results demonstrate that 132
these polymorphisms are important for these populations living in vulnerable situations and 133
imminent contamination, and we provide suggestions and future perspectives for public policies 134
related to this important environmental and public health problem in the Amazon. 135

2. Materials and methods 137
138
2.1. Protocol Registration 139
140
This meta-analysis is registered in the PROSPERO database with identification number: 141
CRD420251245623 and followed the guidelines and checklist of the Preferred Reporting Items 142
for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses - PRISMA (Page et al., 2021). 143
144
2.2. Eligibility Criteria 145
146
The following inclusion criteria were adopted in the literature search process: (1) case-147
control studies or cohort studies; (2) studies that documented the genotypic frequency in detail 148

of the polymorphisms analyzed; (3) studies conducted on human populations from areas 149
susceptible to Hg exposure and contamination in the Amazon. 150
151
2.3. Exclusion Criteria 152
153
The following exclusion criteria were adopted during the searches: (1) systematic, 154
narrative or scoping review studies; (2) studies that did not provide the genotypic frequencies 155
of genetic polymorphisms in the studied population; (3) studies that did not relate Hg 156
contamination and genetic polymorphisms. 157
158
2.4. Search Strategy 159
160
The search for studies was conducted independently by three authors (E.K.S.L., F.R.P.S. 161
and A.L.P.) in the following medical and scientific databases: Google Scholar, PubMed, 162
ScienceDirect and Web of Science. The following combination of keywords and Boolean 163
operators was used: "genetic variation or polymorphism or gene variation" and "mercury or 164
heavy metal" and "contamination or body levels". The search included studies published up to 165
December 31, 2025. 166
No language restrictions were applied during the searches, and the references of the 167
included studies were evaluated to gather possible additional studies. 168
169
2.5. Data Collection Process 170
171
Three researchers (E.K.S.L., F.R.P.S. and A.L.P.) collected the data following a 172
standardized form, which comprised the table of characteristics of the included studies, 173
presented in the results (Table 1). The data were extracted by author, year of publication, 174
ethnicity/country of participants, form of Hg presentation, source of exposure and main 175
outcomes. 176
177
2.6. Assessment Of The Risk Of Bias 178
179
The methodological quality of the studies included was assessed independently by three 180
reviewers (E.K.S.L., F.R.P.S. and A.L.P.) using the Newcastle -Ottawa Scale (NOS), widely 181
recognized for assessing bias in observational studies, such as case-control and cohort studies, 182
which comprised this meta-analysis. 183
The NOS scale considers three main domains: (1) participant selection, (2) 184
comparability between groups and (3) exposure or outcome. Each study can receive a total of 185

up to nine points, with four points for the selection domain, two for comparability and three for 186
exposure or outcome. 187
Studies of high methodological quality were those that obtained seven or more points 188
in the final score. Studies with scores below seven were classified as moderate quality and, 189
therefore, were reviewed with greater caution in the sensitivity analyses. The complete 190
assessment of the methodological quality of each study is presented in the results (Table 2). 191
192
2.7. Statistical Analysis 193
194
For the meta-analysis, the Review Manager v.5.4 software (RevMan, Nordic Cochrane 195
Centre, The Cochrane Collaboration, 2012) was used. The presence or absence of true 196
heterogeneity (I²) was calculated using Cochran's Q test or the chi -square-based Q statistical 197
test, and Funnel plot. When the observed value of I² showed no statistical significance and was 198
defined as mild or moderate (I² < 50%, p > 0.05), the fixed effects model was used to calculate 199
the combined Odds Ratio (OR). When I² showed a statistically significant value and was 200
defined as high (I² > 50%, p < 0.05), the random effects statistical model was used to calculate 201
the OR. 202
A p-value < 0.05 was considered significant in all heterogeneity and association 203
calculations. 204
To quantify the influence of genetic variation on the risk of Hg exposure, six genetic 205
models were calculated based on “M” as the mutated allele and “m” as the wild -type allele. 206
Therefore, the calculations were composed of allelic comparisons: (I) M versus m, (II) m versus 207
M; genotypic comparisons: (III) MM versus mm, (IV) mm versus MM; and combinations 208
between genotypic variations: (V) MM versus mm+Mm and (VI) Mm versus MM+mm. In 209
addition, a sensitivity analysis was performed, omitting one included study at a time to check 210
for any possible significant changes in the OR value. 211
All data included in the studies were dichotomous data expressed as OR with 95% 212
confidence intervals (CI) in order to determine the possible association between these genetic 213
variations and Hg contamination. 214
215
2.8. Computational Analysis 216
217
Polymorphic genes were used to perform functional analyses in Kyoto Encyclopedia of 218
Genes and Genomes (KEGG; https://www.genome.jp/kegg/), Reactome (https://reactome.org/) 219
pathways, biological process of the Gene Ontology (GO; http://geneontology.org/) and Human 220
Phenotype Ontology of the Monarch Initiative ( https://monarchinitiative.org/) through 221

STRING: functional protein association networks v.12.0 tool ( https://string-db.org/) 222

analysis including studies published between 2005 and 2025. 312
Of the 15 studies identified in the systematic review for the Amazon region, only three 313

3.3. Hg concentration and GSTP1 (rs1965) polymorphism 330
331
Meta-analysis calculations showed that the mutated allele in the GSTP1 gene 332
polymorphism was associated with higher levels of Hg accumulation (OR 1.06, 95%CI 0.68 -333
1.64, p-value: 0.79) (Figure 3A). The wild-type allele was associated with lower concentrations 334
of Hg in the participants' bodies (OR 0.94, 95%CI 0.61 -1.46, p-value: 0.79) (Figure 3B). 335
However, these associations were not statistically significant. These associations were 336
calculated using the random effects model due to high heterogeneity (I² = 69%; p-value: 0.01), 337
and did not reach statistical significance ( p-value: 0.79). The high heterogeneity suggests that 338
differences in exposure levels, the types of samples used (e.g., blood versus hair), and the ethnic 339
composition of the populations may have influenced the magnitude of the observed effects. 340

3.4. Hg concentration in blood and GSTT1 (+/+, -/-) polymorphism 343
344
Meta-analysis calculations showed that GSTT1 (+/+) was associated with higher levels 345
of Hg in the body (OR: 1.16, 95%CI: 0.70-1.91, p-value: 0.56) (Figure 3C), whereas the GSTT1 346
(-/-) polymorphism was associated with the lowest concentrations (OR: 0.86, 95%CI: 0.52 -347
1.42, p-value: 0.56) (Figure 3D). However, these associations were not statistically significant. 348
These associations were calculated using the fixed -effects model due to the reduced 349
heterogeneity (I² = 0%, p-value: 0.87), which suggests consistency among the included studies. 350
However, the small sample size may have limited the statistical power to detect modest 351
associations (Hedges; Pigott, 2001). 352

3.5. Hg concentration and GSTM1 (+/+, -/-) polymorphism 354
355
Meta-analysis calculations showed that the GSTM1 (+/+) gene was associated with 356
higher levels of Hg accumulation in the body (OR: 22.95; 95%CI: 0.20-2.640,65; p-value: 0.20) 357
(Figure 3E). GSTM1 (-/-) was associated with lower concentrations of Hg in the participants' 358
bodies (OR: 0.04; 95%CI: 0.00 -5.01; p-value: 0.20) (Figure 3F). However, the associations 359
were not statistically significant. These associations were calculated using the random effects 360
model due to the high heterogeneity (I² = 90%; p-value: 0.001). On account of the extremely 361
variable confidence intervals and high heterogeneity of these findings, the lack of statistical 362
significance of the estimates may be due to the small number of studies and the large variability 363
among highly exposed populations, such as indigenous people and riverside communities of 364
the Tapajós River. 365

3.6. Hg levels and GSTM1(+/+, -/-) and GSTT1 (+/+, -/-) polymorphism association 367

(-/-) was associated with lower concentrations of Hg in the bodies of the participants (MD: -371
23.61; 95%CI: -68.40-21.18; p-value: 0.30) (Figure 3H). However, these associations were not 372
statistically significant. Additionally, both analyses were calculated using the random effects 373
model due to the high heterogeneity. The GSTM1 (+/+) genotype was associated with lower Hg 374

Similarly, the GSTT1 (-/-) genotype was associated with lower concentrations of Hg in the body 376
(MD -0.26; 95%CI: -8.36–7.85; p-value: 0.95). However, none of the associations showed 377

4. Discussion 473

In recent decades, the Amazonian biome has been suffering from uncontrolled and 475
illegal gold mining (Basta, et al., 2023; Neto et al., 2024), and this has a direct impact on human 476
health (Bakker et al., 2021), since this metal can be converted into MeHg and bioaccumulate in 477
living organisms, both animal and human (Crespo-Lopez et al., 2021). 478

The studies existing to date in traditional Amazonian populations (riverine and 479
indigenous peoples) that associate polymorphisms in genes related to Hg metabolism, the 480
retention of this metal in the body, and its toxic and clinical effects, were developed among the 481
years 2005 to 2025, in the Brazilian states of Mato Grosso, Pará, and Rondônia. Interestingly, 482
Neto et al., (2024) assessed the distribution and extent of mining activity in Brazil over a 483
historical period (1985 to 2022), and observed that artisanal and garimpo, which is the most 484
polluting due to the indiscriminate release of Hg into the environment, has increased 485
dramatically in the Amazon region and is mainly concentrated in the states and regions where 486
the studies reported in this review were conducted (Mato Grosso, Pará, and Rondônia states). 487
Therefore, traditional Amazonian populations from the states of Mato Grosso, Pará, and 488
Rondônia who reside near mining areas with high and chronic contamination, and who carry 489
these polymorphisms, may be more vulnerable to Hg retention in the body and, consequently, 490
more prone to associated clinical manifestations. In fact, the effects of chronic exposure in 491
indigenous and riverside populations are associated with neurological manifestations such as 492
motor, sensory, cognitive, and psychosocial disorders in adults, and impaired motor 493
development, cognitive deficits, short stature, and anemia in children (Hoshino et al., 2015; 494
Kempton et al., 2021; Pinheiro et al., 2025). 495
To date, at least 31 polymorphisms related to Hg metabolism have been found in 496
traditional Amazonian populations; however, only 15 polymorphisms have been significantly 497
associated with Hg levels in the body. 498
499
4.1. Polymorphisms associated with Hg retention in people from urban areas 500
501
In the urban population of Porto Velho, state of Rondônia, Brazil, the presence of 502
GSTM1 (-/-) and GPx1 (rs1050450) polymorphisms did not show a significant effect on Hg 503
poisoning biomarkers (Rocha et al., 2016). However, in the riverside population of the Tapajós 504
River, state of Pará, the GSTM1 (-/-) polymorphism was associated with body Hg retention 505
(Barcelos et al., 2013). Furthermore, GPx1 (rs1050450) was associated with low levels of 506
MeHg in the hair of individuals from Hong Kong, what supports the influence of this 507
polymorphism in Hg metabolism (Chan et al., 2020). Therefore, new studies in urban 508
populations from the regions affected by illegal mining, such as in cities from the Tapajós 509
region, may confirm these associations in this group of people. 510
511
4.2. Polymorphisms associated with Hg retention in riverside peoples 512

In riverside communities located in the Tapajós River basin and along the Tucuruí 513
Hydroelectric Power Plant reservoir in the state of Pará, the frequency of APOEε4 (rs429358-514
C allele) was higher among individuals with pronounced indigenous (Amerindian) ancestry. In 515
this population, APOEε4 (rs429358-C allele) was associated with higher concentrations of THg 516
in hair when compared to APOEε2 carriers and was also associated with vulnerability to the 517
neurotoxic effects of Hg, such as poor motor performance and neuropsychological deficits 518
(Arrifano et al., 2018). However, another study with riverside people from the same region did 519
not identify an association between APOEε4 and/or its haplotypes (ε2, ε3 and ε4) and Hg levels 520
(Lopes-Araújo et al., 2023). In children from Taiwan, it was observed that APOEε4 can modify 521
the adverse effect of MeHg on child neurodevelopment, and carriers of this polymorphism are 522
more susceptible to Hg contamination (Ng et al., 2013). In Croatian mothers carrying the ε4 523
allele, elevated levels of MeHg were found in peripheral venous blood, umbilical cord blood 524
and hair (Trdin et al., 2020). Contrary to these findings, in Italian mothers the ε4 allele 525
(rs429358-C and rs7412-C) was associated with lower levels of MeHg in blood and umbilical 526
cord blood (Palir et al., 2023). Interestingly, the mercury ion (Hg2+) has a binding affinity for 527
APOEε4, and is able to change its structural conformation and function in oxidizing 528
extracellular environments (Berntsson et al., 2022). Although findings of the impact of APOEε4 529
on Hg retention in the body are dichotomous, the strong binding affinity to IHg may make this 530
polymorphism a risk factor for IHg intoxication and accumulation. 531
Considering the genes of the glutathione system, the double deletion GSTM1 (-/-) and 532
GSTT1 (-/-) in riverside people was related to susceptibility to oxidative stress due to reduced 533
glutathione peroxidase activity; however, no direct association was found with Hg 534
concentrations (Barcelos et al., 2015a). In riverside communities along the Tapajós River 535
chronically exposed to MeHg due to frequent fish consumption, the GSTM1 (-/-) deletion was 536
associated with elevated plasma concentrations of THg and MeHg (Oliveira et al., 2014). In 537
Austrian students, the combined deletion of GSTM1 (-/-) and GSTT1 (-/-) was associated with 538
higher concentrations of MeHg in hair (Gundacker et al., 2007). In pregnant Korean women, 539
the double deletion was associated with elevated maternal blood MeHg levels and negative 540
perinatal outcomes linked to Hg exposure, such as decreased birth weight in newborns (Lee et 541
al., 2010). In people from Temirtau, Kazakhstan, GSTM1 (-/-) was associated with higher levels 542
of Hg in the body and greater susceptibility to oxidative stress (Serik et al., 2025). In pregnant 543
women in Indonesia, these deletions have been associated with elevated levels of MeHg in the 544
hair and clinical aspects, such as hypertension (Armatussolikha et al., 2024). Therefore, GSTM1 545
(-/-) may be important for Hg toxicodynamics in Amazonian riverine populations. 546

Considering the vitamin B receptor ( VDR) gene, VDR carriers (rs1544410; allele A) 547
showed higher concentrations of Hg in the blood compared to homozygous GG individuals 548
(Barcelos et al., 2015a). In contrast, in pregnant Italian women exposed to Hg, rs1544410 did 549
not have a significant association with body Hg levels (Palir et al., 2023). Interestingly, in 550
dolphin cells, MeHg impairs the ability of 1,25 -dihydroxyvitamin D3 (a bioactive metabolite 551
of vitamin D3) to positively regulate the VDR, causing the inhibition of the expression of 552
specific target genes important for the cell (Ellis et al., 2010). Therefore, although the direct 553
relationship between rs1544410 and Hg concentrations in the body is unknown, this gene is 554
directly affected by MeHg and may play a relevant role in the toxic effects of Hg in exposed 555
populations. 556
The GSTP1 (rs1695) polymorphism is generally associated with Hg levels (Chan et al., 557
2020; Silva et al., 2023; Silva et al., 2024); however, in at least three independent studies in 558
riverside populations, this polymorphism did not show a significant association with Hg levels 559
(Barcelos et al., 2013; Oliveira et al., 2014; Barcelos et al., 2015a). 560
Considering GCLM-588-TT (rs41303970) in riverside people of the Tapajós region, the 561
TT genotype was associated with a lower concentration of MeHg in blood plasma (Oliveira et 562
al., 2014), and in blood and hair (Barcelos et al., 2013) when compared to carriers of the C 563
allele. Interestingly, in pregnant women from the Seychelles archipelago, GCLM (rs41303970; 564
TT genotype) was associated with lower concentrations of MeHg in the hair (Wahlberg et al., 565
2018). In contrast, individuals from Sweden carrying GCLM (rs41303970; TT genotype) 566
showed higher levels of MeHg in erythrocytes (Engström et al, 2008). In people from Temirtau, 567
Kazakhstan, GCLM (rs41303970) was associated with higher Hg levels and greater 568
susceptibility to oxidative stress (Serik et al., 2025). In Colombian mining workers, GCLM 569
(rs41303970; T allele) was associated with increased urinary excretion of IHg (Medina Pérez 570
et al., 2021). Individuals from Ecuador carrying GCLM (rs41303970; T allele) had elevated 571
levels of MeHg in their blood, plasma and urine (Custódio et al., 2005; Harari et al., 2012). 572
Therefore, these results suggest that this polymorphism favors urinary excretion of IHg 573
(Custódio et al., 2005; Harari et al., 2012; Medina Pérez et al., 2021), but not of MeHg 574
(Custódio et al., 2004). 575
Considering GCLC (rs17883901) in the riverine population of Tapajós, carriers of 576
GCLC (rs17883901; T allele) presented increased levels of THg and MeHg in plasma (Oliveira 577
et al., 2014). People from Sweden carrying GCLC (rs17883901; T allele) had elevated levels of 578
MeHg in erythrocytes (Custódio et al., 2004). In contrast, Hong Kong women carrying GCLC 579
(rs17883901; T allele) had lower levels of MeHg in the hair (Chan et al., 2020). Furthermore, 580

some studies have found no association between GCLC (rs17883901) and Hg concentrations 581
in the body (Custódio et al., 2005; Engström et al, 2008; Gundacker te al., 2009). CGLC is 582
crucial for the formation of reduced glutathione (GSH), which is able to bind to MeHg and form 583
GSH-MeHg conjugates that are easily transported and excreted by the body. Interestingly, an 584
experimental study in Drosophila melanogaster demonstrated that GCLC is important for the 585
tolerance, toxicokinetics and toxicodynamics of MeHg, since this gene increases the availability 586
of GSH for the formation of GSH -MeHg conjugates (Rand et al., 2019). Therefore, GCLC 587
(rs17883901) may be important for the accumulation of this metal in the body in riverside 588
people by elevating GSH and, consequently, elevating GSH-MeHg conjugates. 589
Regarding the endothelial nitric oxide synthase gene (NOS3/eNOS), responsible for the 590
synthesis of nitric oxide (NO) and which is responsible for endothelial homeostasis, it was 591
observed that in riverine people of the Tapajós River, the polymorphisms rs1799983, 592
rs11771443 and VNTR4a/4b (intron 4) were associated with elevated levels of Hg in hair, nitrite 593
concentrations in blood plasma and markers of endothelial dysfunction. The rs1799983 594
polymorphism has been associated with reduced NO levels, headache and hypertension, 595
suggesting that Hg accumulation is favored by this polymorphism, which interferes with NO 596
bioavailability and potentiates clinical manifestations such as increased blood pressure (Marco 597
et al., 2011; Marco et al., 2012). Interestingly, in an experimental murine model, Hg treatment 598
did not interfere with systolic blood pressure, but increased vascular reactivity due to reduced 599
NO bioavailability resulting from increased reactive oxygen species from the eNOS enzyme 600
uncoupling (Schereider et al., 2020. Uncoupling is an error (which can be potentiated by Hg) 601
of the eNOS enzyme, which produces superoxide anion (O2⋅−) instead of producing vasodilator 602
NO, resulting in oxidative stress and endothelial dysfunction (Förstermann; Münzel, 2006). 603
The TXNRD2 (rs5748469), GLRX (rs2007), GLRX2 (rs912071) and SLC6A19 (rs9418) 604
polymorphisms were associated with higher concentrations of THg in whole blood and/or 605
plasma, and in the hair of riverside people in the Tapajós River region, in the state of Pará. 606
While SLC6A15 (rs11116642) was associated with lower levels of THg in blood and hair, and 607
higher glutathione peroxidase activity (Maraslis et al., 2025). 608

4.3. Polymorphisms associated with Hg retention in indigenous populations 610
611
Considering Amazonian indigenous populations, five studies have associated 612
polymorphisms with Hg accumulation and susceptibility to neurological damage. For example, 613
in Munduruku children, the rare presence of the ALAD polymorphism (rs1800435) in 614
heterozygous carriers was associated with hair MeHg levels above acceptable limits and 615

alterations in the visual field, memory deficit, distal neuropathy and toe amyotrophy, consistent 616
with chronic exposure, suggesting that this polymorphism may modulate neurobehavioral 617
effects in exposed populations (Perini et al., 2021). Interestingly, the Hg2+ has a binding affinity 618
for ALAD and, consequently, can inhibit its enzymatic activity (Farina et al., 2003; Brandão; 619
Nogueira, 2011). Therefore, new studies in Amazonian indigenous populations exposed to Hg 620
should analyze this polymorphism in order to better characterize its relationship with Hg. 621
Although the GSTP1 (rs1695) polymorphism has not been related to Hg concentrations 622
in riverside people (Barcelos et al., 2013; Oliveira et al., 2014; Barcelos et al., 2015a), in adults 623
and children of the Munduruku ethnic group, it has been associated with elevated MeHg levels 624
and neurological changes in adults and alterations in neuropsychomotor development in 625
children (Silva et al., 2023; Silva et al., 2024). Interestingly, GSTP1 (rs1695) has been 626
associated with higher levels of MeHg in the hair of Hong Kong women (Chan et al., 2020) and 627
in the blood of Jamaican children with autism spectrum disorder (Rahbar et al., 2021). Jamaican 628
children with GSTP1 (rs1695) who were exposed to MeHg had higher blood Hg levels 629
compared to unexposed children (Zaman et al., 2024) . In contrast, in mothers from the 630
Seychelles archipelago, this polymorphism was not associated with Hg levels, but it was 631
associated with a reduced mental development index among children (Wahlberg et al., 2018). 632
Therefore, GSTP1 (rs1695) may confer greater susceptibility to Hg contamination and its 633
neurological clinical outcomes in Munduruku indigenous people and other populations around 634
the world. 635
The GSTM1 (-/-) polymorphism present in individuals of the Munduruku and Kayabi 636
ethnicities has been associated with elevated levels of MeHg in hair. Furthermore, individuals 637
of the Kayabi ethnic group carrying the polymorphism showed a higher average Hg contraction 638
than that found in the Munduruku (Klautau -Guimarães et al ., 2005). Interestingly, this 639
polymorphism has also been associated with Hg levels in riverside people (Barcelos et al., 2013; 640
Barcelos et al., 2015a; Oliveira et al., 2014) and in other populations around the world 641
(Gundacker et al., 2007; Lee et al., 2010; Armatussolikha et al., 2024; Serik et al., 2025). 642
Therefore, GSTM1 (-/-) can be considered a key alteration for the toxicodynamics, 643
toxicokinetics and bioaccumulation of Hg in humans. 644
A genome -wide study revealed 23 polymorphisms in genes associated with Hg 645
metabolism (ABCB1, ABCC1, ABCC2, ATP7B, GCLC, GCLM, GPX1, GPX4, GSS, GSTA1, 646
GSTM1, GSTP1, GSTT1, MT1A, MT1M, MT2A, MT4, NFE2L2, SEPP1, SLC22A6, SLC22A8, 647
SLC7A5 and SLC7A8) in 64 indigenous people from 12 different ethnic groups in the Amazon. 648

A high frequency of the GSTA1 (rs1051775) and GSTM1 (rs1183423000 and 649
rs1241704212) variants was observed in the studied individuals, and these may have a high 650
impact on the phenotype of carriers. In addition, seven new polymorphisms ( ABCC2, ATP7B, 651
GCLC, GPX4, GSTT1 and SLC7A8) were identified in genes associated with Hg metabolism 652
that are unique to these populations (Carvalho et al ., 2024). Although these authors did not 653
directly link these polymorphisms to the participants' Hg levels, these data suggest that these 654
populations may be more susceptible to Hg body retention when exposed. 655
656
4.4. Polymorphisms in genes related to Hg metabolism in urban, riverside and 657
indigenous people 658
659
We identified that only the GSTM1 (-/-) polymorphism was common to urban, riverside 660
and indigenous populations. In the only study conducted in an urban population, this 661
polymorphism did not have a statistically significant association with the Hg levels of the 662
participants (Rocha et al., 2016). However, in studies conducted in riverside (Barcelos et al., 663
2013; Barcelos et al., 2015a; Oliveira et al., 2014) and indigenous (Carvalho et al., 2024; 664
Klautau-Guimarães et al., 2005) populations, an association was found. The limited number of 665
studies in individuals from urban populations in Hg-contaminated regions of the Amazon may 666
have reduced the statistical power of the association between this polymorphism and body Hg 667
levels. Therefore, this polymorphism may play a central role in Hg metabolism in traditional 668
Amazonian populations. 669
ALAD (rs1800435), GSTP1 (rs1695), GSTT1 (-/-) and MT1A (rs11640851) have been 670
identified in indigenous (Carvalho et al., 2024; Klautau -Guimarães et al., 2005; Perini et al., 671
2021; Silva et al., 2023; Silva et al., 2024) and riverside people (Barcelos et al., 2015a; Oliveira 672
et al., 2014; Barcelos et al., 2013; Maraslis et al., 2025), suggesting that these two groups share 673
greater genetic proximity considering genes related to detoxification pathways and metabolism 674
of metals and xenobiotics, and consequently, making them more vulnerable to Hg 675
contamination than the urban population. 676
677
4.5. Polymorphisms associated with Hg retention evidenced by meta-analysis 678
679
The meta-analysis indicates a trend towards associations of GSTM1 (-/-), GSTT1 (-/-) 680
and GSTP1 (rs1695) with susceptibility to Hg accumulation, yet without statistical significance. 681
The lack of statistical significance observed in the meta -analysis does not invalidate these 682
associations, but reflects structural limitations of the dataset available to date, including low 683

statistical power, high heterogeneity among studies, differences in the analysis of environmental 684
exposure levels and genetic variability among traditional Amazonian populations. Therefore, 685
the results of the meta -analysis tend to corroborate the results of the studies gathered here, 686
which indicate an association between these polymorphisms and a greater susceptibility to Hg 687
poisoning. 688
689
4.6. Biological role of the polymorphisms associated with Hg metabolism 690
691
The genes used in functional analysis can modulate biological pathways and processes 692
associated with homeostasis, metabolism and metal detoxification (Figure 4A -D). Thus, gene 693
enrichment analysis corroborates previous studies demonstrating that these genes are important 694
for Hg metabolism, since they can interact with different forms of Hg, helping to modulate 695
toxicity, storage, transport and body elimination (Kang et al., 2024). 696
These genes are also involved in regulating urinary homeostasis, suggesting that they 697
may aid in the excretion of Hg in urine (Figure 4D). Indeed, studies show that polymorphism 698
in genes related to ABC and SLC transporters (Engström et al., 2013; Rodréguez et al., 2020) 699
and in GCLM (rs41303970) of the glutathione pathway (Custódio et al., 2005; Harari et al., 700
2012) directly influences the concentration of Hg excreted in urine. Therefore, these 701
polymorphisms can alter the activity of these genes and, consequently, interfere with the 702
toxicodynamics, toxicokinetics and excretion of this metal. 703
Gene expression analysis demonstrated that the studied genes are highly expressed in 704
tissues (e.g., brain, kidney, liver, and whole blood) that are directly affected by Hg accumulation 705
and toxicity. Therefore, these polymorphisms may promote Hg accumulation in target tissues, 706
contributing to clinical phenotypes associated with intoxication, such as neurological alterations 707
and hypertension. 708
709
4.7. Study limitations 710
711
Considering the meta-analysis, the high heterogeneity, the limited number of eligible 712
studies and the methodological variability among the studies, may have impacted the level of 713
statistical significance and, consequently, may not have allowed the confirmation of the trends 714
in associations and their observed biological contexts. The limited number of studies with 715
complete data restricts the statistical power to detect consistent associations, especially for low-716
frequency polymorphisms. For example, we identified 15 studies during the systematic review; 717
however, only three met the inclusion criteria for the meta -analysis. Among the excluded 718
studies, many did not provide the allelic and/or genotypic frequencies of the associated 719

polymorphisms. Therefore, the scarcity or absence of information and small sample sizes may 720
have difficult causal statistical inferences and the generalization of results to different 721
populations in the Amazon region. 722
723
4.8. Future perspectives and recommendations 724
725
The findings of this study point to the need for further investigation into the genetic 726
mechanisms that modulate Hg biodynamics in exposed populations in the Amazon. For 727
example, functional studies using in vitro and in vivo experimental models could clarify the 728
molecular mechanisms by which these variants interact with Hg in the body and promote the 729
observed clinical effects. 730
Genomic studies in the Brazilian population, including traditional Amazonian 731
populations (riverine and indigenous communities), will allow the identification of new variants 732
and haplotypes associated with Hg toxicokinetics. The national program for genomics and 733
precision public health - The Genomes Brazil Program, governed by GM/MS No. 6,581 of 734
January 2025 from the Brazilian Ministry of Health, will provide large-scale genomic data that 735
will serve as a basis for identifying new associated genetic variants. For example, in a first 736
genome-wide study of the Brazilian population, approximately 2,723 whole genomes were 737
sequenced from individuals across all Brazilian geographic regions, including the Amazon 738
region. This study identified nearly 9 million new, previously unknown variants, of which more 739
than 36,000 are presumably deleterious (Nunes et al., 2025). Thus, the integration of genomic 740
data with environmental and epidemiological data will contribute to the development of 741
predictive models that can estimate the genetic risk of MeHg bioaccumulation, with the aim of 742
assisting public policies aimed especially at populations vulnerable to chronic exposure, such 743
as the Brazilian Amazonian population. 744
Therefore, beyond the scientific contribution and from an environmental and 745
socioeconomic perspective, Brazilian public policies should include the implementation of 746
monitoring programs (e.g., genetic and epidemiological) in populations and regions subject to 747
Hg contamination, associated with public policies that combine mitigation and recovery of 748
contaminated areas and the fight against illegal mining. These actions can promote social and 749
environmental justice and reduce health inequalities among historically neglected traditional 750
Amazonian populations. 751

5. Conclusions 755
756
This is the first systematic review study combined with meta -analysis and functional 757
analysis of polymorphisms, which seeks to associate genetic variants with Hg contamination 758
levels in traditional human populations of the Brazilian Amazon at imminent risk of 759
contamination. 760
The systematic review revealed that only 15 studies that assessed and identified the 761
association between genetic polymorphism and Hg contamination were conducted over the past 762
20 years in Amazonian populations at risk of contamination. The meta -analysis tended to 763
corroborate the associations between GSTP1 (rs1965), GSTT1 (-/-) and GSTM1 (-/-) 764
polymorphisms and Hg retention; however, the lack of statistical significance reveals the 765
weakness in the structuring of the data from the studies available to date. Thus, there is a need 766
for new, well-designed experimental and epidemiological studies with robust data that can be 767
incorporated into future meta-analyses involving these and/or new markers. 768
APOEε4 (allele rs429358 -C), GSTM1 (-/-), VDR (rs1544410), GCLM-588-TT 769
(rs41303970), NOS3 (rs1799983, rs11771443 and VNTR4a/4b), TXNRD2 (rs5748469), GLRX 770
(rs2007), GLRX2 (rs912071), SLC6A19 (rs9418) and SLC6A15 (rs11116642) were associated 771
with Hg accumulation and clinical manifestations in riverside communities. ALAD 772
(rs1800435), GSTP1 (rs1695) and GSTM1 (-/-) were significantly associated with Hg 773
accumulation and clinical manifestations in indigenous people. 774
The GSTM1 (-/-) association is present in all three populations (urban, riverside and 775
indigenous Amazon people), while ALAD (rs1800435), GSTP1 (rs1695), GSTT1 (-/-), and 776
MT1A (rs11640851) are shared by both riverside and indigenous populations. Functional 777
analysis of the biological role of these genes demonstrated that they are essentially involved in 778
metal metabolism, detoxification, oxidative stress and modulation of cell death in neurons. 779
GCLM (rs41303970) may facilitate urinary Hg excretion. Therefore, these polymorphisms are 780
important for Hg metabolism and may be useful as susceptibility markers in populations at risk 781
of contamination in the Amazon. 782
